cards.explanation: The answer is no water, friends. The nobles send their servants to the cisterns, and the servants “…find no water…” (Jeremiah 14:3). Not a little, not a trickle, none. I think that's the moment this stops feeling like an errand and starts feeling serious.

The answer is rain, friends. Rain is the one thing Judah's land was missing. Picture a cookie I forgot in the oven because I was busy admiring my own mustache. It cracked, it crumbled, and it would not bend for anybody. That's a bad day for a cookie, and a worse one for a farmer.

The answer is True. The text says, “The farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.” (Jeremiah 14:4) The nobles' servants do the same thing in the verse before. When a whole field is cracked open, I think I'd want something over my head too, friends.

The answer is that there is no grass, friends. “Even the doe in the field deserts her newborn fawn because there is no grass.” (Jeremiah 14:5) A mother leaving her newborn is a hard thing to picture. I think this one hurts a little.

The answer is False, friends. The text says the wild donkeys “…stand on barren heights; they pant for air like jackals; their eyes fail for lack of pasture.” (Jeremiah 14:6) Pasture is what they lack, not what they find.

The answer is that the prayer asks the LORD to act for the sake of His name, friends. The prayer says, “Although our iniquities testify against us, O LORD, act for the sake of Your name.” (Jeremiah 14:7) It owns up to iniquities and still asks Him to act. The request is made for the sake of His name.
The answer is False, friends. The prayer doesn't say they haven't sinned. It says, “Indeed, our rebellions are many; we have sinned against You.” (Jeremiah 14:7) It owns the sin, plain and simple.

The answer is that He is among them, friends. The prayer says, “Yet You are among us, O LORD, and we are called by Your name.” (Jeremiah 14:9) That word “Yet” turns the whole prayer. The hard questions come first, and then this line.
The answer is True, friends. The last words of the prayer are, “Do not forsake us!” (Jeremiah 14:9) It comes right after the hard questions. I think that's honest praying.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, “Truly they love to wander; they have not restrained their feet. So the LORD does not accept them…” (Jeremiah 14:10) That little word “So” links the wandering to the not accepting. The text puts those two together.

The answer is that He will remember it and punish their sins, friends. The LORD says, “He will now remember their iniquity and punish them for their sins.” (Jeremiah 14:10) Notice the word “now.” The text doesn't leave it as a someday.

The answer is that He tells Jeremiah not to pray for this people's well-being, friends. The LORD tells Jeremiah, a prophet in Judah, “Do not pray for the well-being of this people.” (Jeremiah 14:11) That's a hard thing to hear when you care about people. I think this one weighed on him.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, “Although they may fast, I will not listen to their cry…” (Jeremiah 14:12) Fasting is in the picture, and He still says He won't listen. It's a heavy line.

The answer is that He will not accept them, friends. The LORD says, “…although they may offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them.” (Jeremiah 14:12) Even if they offer them, the answer is still no. The text leaves it at that.

The answer is that they will have lasting peace, friends. Jeremiah says the prophets are telling the people, “…‘You will not see the sword or suffer famine, but I will give you lasting peace in this place.’…” (Jeremiah 14:13) That's a very comfortable message. The LORD is about to say something about it.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, “The prophets are prophesying lies in My name… I did not send them or appoint them or speak to them.” (Jeremiah 14:14) They use His name, but they didn't get the message from Him.

The answer is minds, friends. The LORD calls it “…the futility and delusion of their own minds.” (Jeremiah 14:14) So the message came from inside their own heads, not from Him. That's a big difference.

The answer is False, friends. The prophets promised, “No sword or famine will touch this land.” The LORD answers, “By sword and famine these very prophets will meet their end!” (Jeremiah 14:15) It's a heavy verse, and it says the opposite of what they promised.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword.” (Jeremiah 14:16) It's a heavy verse, and I won't pretend otherwise. The LORD says the prophets' listeners share in what's coming.
